name: CortiSlim

lead: CortiSlim is a brand of weight-loss supplements marketed around lowering the stress hormone cortisol. People bought it hoping to lose weight, especially around the midsection.

The marketing idea was that stress-related cortisol promotes fat storage and that herbal blends of magnolia bark, green tea and banana leaf extracts could modulate cortisol, appetite and blood sugar. No studies were found showing the product changes cortisol or body weight, and the FTC found its claims of supporting research to be false.

paras: Taken as pills in a diet or stress-management routine, usually alongside calorie control. The brand was sold by CortiSlim International and earlier by Window Rock Enterprises, and was acquired in 2008.

Ingredients include bitter orange (synephrine), green tea extract and vanadyl sulfate, each with its own safety considerations. The marketing was the subject of FTC action and the original marketer went bankrupt.

angle.text: CortiSlim was marketed to people wanting to lose midsection fat by controlling cortisol. No published trials test the product, and its advertising drew an FTC action.

lead: CortiSlim is a branded dietary supplement line that was marketed as a "cortisol control" weight-loss formula. It was sold by CortiSlim International and earlier by Window Rock Enterprises, and it combined several herbal blends such as magnolia bark, green tea extract and banana leaf extract [1].

The product was marketed on the idea that stress-related cortisol promotes fat storage. The US Federal Trade Commission challenged advertising for cortisol-related weight-loss products, and Wikipedia reports that the marketer lost a false-advertising case and later went bankrupt; the line was acquired in 2008 [1]. No independent clinical trials of the product were found.
infobox: FTC false-advertising action; Window Rock Enterprises bankrupt [1]

paras: Wikipedia lists three blends. Cortiplex contains magnolia bark extract, beta-sitosterol and L-theanine; Leptiplex contains green tea extract and bitter orange (synephrine); Insutrol contains banana leaf extract and vanadyl sulfate. The formula also includes vitamin C, calcium and chromium [1]. Promoters said Cortiplex keeps cortisol within a healthy range, Leptiplex helps control appetite, and Insutrol balances blood sugar [1]. Under a settlement, the current owner no longer describes the product as a cortisol antagonist [1].

The FTC determined that promoters' claims of more than 15 years of scientific research supporting the product were false [1]. Wikipedia reports a fine in 2007, but its sources give conflicting amounts, and the original owner went into bankruptcy [1].
